passages.original: Fuit autem et animo magno et corpore imperatoriaque forma, ut ipso aspectu cuivis iniceret admirationem sui, sed in labore nimis remissus parumque patiens, ut Theopompus memoriae prodidit, bonus vero civis fideque magna. quod cum in aliis rebus declaravit, tum maxime in Amyntae Macedonis liberis tuendis. namque Eurydice, mater Perdiccae et Philippi, cum his duobus pueris Amynta mortuo ad Iphicraten confugit eiusque opibus defensa est.
passages.english: He was a man of great spirit and great body, and of a commander's bearing, so that by his very appearance he would inspire admiration of himself in anyone; but in exertion he was too slack and had little endurance, as Theopompus has recorded, yet he was a good citizen and of great loyalty. This he showed both in other matters and above all in protecting the children of Amyntas the Macedonian. For Eurydice, the mother of Perdiccas and Philip, fled with these two boys to Iphicrates after Amyntas died, and was defended by his resources.
passages.notes: Nepos's description of Iphicrates as "nimis remissus parumque patiens" in labour is often taken as contradicting other accounts of his vigour; "patiens" is rendered here as "endurance".
